effectivity: standard fuel system: rigid aluminum tank in each wing, 21.5 gal each (43 total / 40 usable, Fig 1-1); the wet-wing integral bays (Figs 12-8/12-9, optional from 17274010) are NOT on this airplane
Fig 12-2 sheet 2 (beginning 17275035) installation; selector drain valve in the valve bottom (beginning 17275035, 12-13)
extra quick drain in each tank's lower outboard corner (17267585 and on / SK172-116, 12-6)
standard one-cylinder primer to cylinder No. 4 (12-2, 12-23); the optional three-cylinder primer is not modelled
carbureted O-320-D2J, gravity feed: no fuel pump (the auxiliary electric and engine-driven pumps of Fig 12-1 sheet 2 / Fig 12-8 sheet 3 are 172Q only)

meta.gravity_feed: No engine-driven or electric fuel pump on the 172P: fuel flows by gravity. Cessna D2065-3-13 12-2 (pdf 328): 'Fuel flows by gravity from two aluminum tanks ... to a four-position selector valve, through an electric auxiliary fuel pump (172Q) through a firewall-mounted fuel strainer to the carburetor and engine primer' (the pump is 172Q only; Fig 12-1 sheet 1, the 172 schematic, has none, sheet 2 with the pumps is the 172Q). The O-320-D2J fuel pump pad is blanked by cover 03D23350 (engine-full.js engine.fuelpump_cover).

strainer on the firewall in the lower engine compartment; inlet elbow through the firewall; drain control beside the oil dipstick (12-19, Fig 12-6)

flow.primer_note: While priming, the plunger draws fuel from the strainer (primer_supply) and pushes it to the cylinder 4 intake port (primer_delivery). Fuel reaches the strainer only with the selector ON (by_selector[pos] segments up to 'strainer'); with OFF the primer draws only what is left in the strainer.
flow.direction: each segment's tube points run in the flow direction (from -> to) except the vent lines (air, either way)
flow.vent_note: vent segments carry air, not fuel: the left tank breathes through the overboard vent line (check valve) and the right tank through its vented cap; the crossover and interconnects tie the airspaces and the aft supply lines together.
flow.gravity_feed: No engine-driven or electric fuel pump on the 172P: fuel flows by gravity. Cessna D2065-3-13 12-2 (pdf 328): 'Fuel flows by gravity from two aluminum tanks ... to a four-position selector valve, through an electric auxiliary fuel pump (172Q) through a firewall-mounted fuel strainer to the carburetor and engine primer' (the pump is 172Q only; Fig 12-1 sheet 1, the 172 schematic, has none, sheet 2 with the pumps is the 172Q). The O-320-D2J fuel pump pad is blanked by cover 03D23350 (engine-full.js engine.fuelpump_cover).
